notes: gigas: genitive plural gigantum
cogitatio: genitive plural cogitationum
cor: i-stem, genitive plural cordium, neuter plural corda
finis: i-stem, genitive plural finium
bitumen: genitive plural bituminum, neuter plural bitumina
summitas: genitive plural summitatum
latus, lateris (side): genitive plural laterum, neuter plural latera; distinct from latus, lata, latum (wide)
fœdus, fœderis (covenant): genitive plural fœderum, neuter plural fœdera; distinct from fœdus, fœda, fœdum (foul)
longitudo, latitudo, altitudo: genitive plural in -inum
bini, binæ, bina: distributive numeral, plural by nature like duo
viginti, quinquaginta: indeclinable numerals
pœnitet, pœnitere, pœnituit: impersonal — third singular only, with the person affected in the accusative (pœnituit eum)
inquam: defective — chiefly inquit, and always placed after the first words it quotes
cœpi, cœpisse: defective — perfect forms only
tollo, tollere, sustuli, sublatus: the perfect and supine are suppletive, borrowed from suffero
mando, mandere, mandi, mansus (to chew) is distinct from mando, mandare (to entrust); mandi here is the present passive infinitive
procreassent (v.1) is syncopated for procreavissent
tecum is cum welded onto the ablative te; the preposition follows the pronoun rather than preceding it
quam in v.21 is the correlative of tam, not the relative pronoun; it is filed under the relative because they are one surface form
cum is two words: the preposition with the ablative, cited 'cum (preposition)' to keep it apart from the conjunction, and the conjunction with the subjunctive. Both are correct on their own tokens.
